event: Modified MI / Battle and Capture of Midway

information_phase.US_first_carrier_force_sighting: center 1942-06-10 05:20-05:50 by Midway PBY; Japanese force assessed as at least 4, probably 5 carriers.
information_phase.Japanese_US_carrier_sighting: center 1942-06-10 06:00-06:30 by overlapping D4Y/B5N/E13A search and recontact; 2 carriers initially, about 3 within 20-30 minutes.
information_phase.relative_information: US has about 20-40 minute first-sighting edge; Japan nevertheless obtains an actionable three-carrier track much earlier/more reliably than historical Midway.
information_phase.why: on-time scout launches + more search legs + layered recontact + better report structure + bounded weather-aware sector overlap; not clairvoyance or perfect forecast.

carrier_air_battle.US_first_wave: about 135-145 aircraft from Enterprise/Hornet/Saratoga, 1942-06-10 06:35-07:20 launch window.
carrier_air_battle.Japanese_first_anti_ship_wave: about 95-102 aircraft, 1942-06-10 06:40-07:10; anti-ship reserve already armed/organized, so historical rearm trap is largely absent.

US_carrier_damage_after_first_exchange.Enterprise: center 1 torpedo + 2 bombs; flight operations stopped, speed reduced.
US_carrier_damage_after_first_exchange.Saratoga: center 2 torpedoes + 1 bomb; flight operations stopped, speed roughly 10-13 kt.
US_carrier_damage_after_first_exchange.Hornet: center 1 torpedo + 1 bomb initially; later additional 2 torpedoes + 1 bomb, flight operations fully stopped.

Japanese_carrier_damage_after_US_strikes.Kaga: about 3 bomb hits; catastrophic fires; eventual loss.
Japanese_carrier_damage_after_US_strikes.Akagi: initial about 1 bomb hit/near miss damage, then about 2 additional bomb hits; catastrophic fires; eventual loss.
Japanese_carrier_damage_after_US_strikes.Soryu: about 2 bomb hits plus near-miss effects; flight-deck mission kill and heavy damage, but fire controlled and ship survives on current most-likely line.
Japanese_carrier_damage_after_US_strikes.Hiryu: about 1 bomb hit + near-miss effects; flight-deck mission kill/heavy damage, ship survives.
Japanese_carrier_damage_after_US_strikes.Zuikaku: no direct hit on current most-likely line; remains operational.

carrier_air_battle.US_TBD: about 34-39 committed; about 25-32 lost; center no torpedo hit on Japanese carriers.
carrier_air_battle.airgroup_survival_rule: Because many Japanese anti-ship aircraft were airborne before carrier damage, carrier hull loss does not equal aircrew/aircraft loss. Surviving aircraft divert to Zuikaku, Ryujo/Junyo, other decks where feasible, Midway/land bases for US aircraft, or ditch with rescue. Reorganization still costs time/cohesion.

surface_pursuit.US_decision: Abandon/tow-attempt Hornet only briefly; split Enterprise and Saratoga on divergent escape routes rather than bind all ships to the slowest carrier.
surface_pursuit.Japanese_decision: Use fast surface forces as planned second-stage kill mechanism; avoid wasting main force on already-stopped Hornet. Air contact from surviving decks narrows escape corridors.
surface_pursuit.combat_effects: Improved practical speed maintenance, night contact/formation handling, surface-torpedo accuracy and 12-20 minute class second-salvo cycle are treated as system effects, not a small generic hit-rate bonus.

US_carrier_fates.Hornet: Abandoned after failed/aborted towing effort; short Japanese boarding/inspection if safe, then scuttled/sunk.
US_carrier_fates.Saratoga: Caught at night after slowed by air damage; screen suffers heavy torpedo/gunfire damage; additional 2-3 Type 93 torpedo hits plus gunfire make loss unavoidable.
US_carrier_fates.Enterprise: Best escape chance, but re-found around dawn; additional carrier-air attack slows/stops her and second pursuing surface group finishes the ship.

surface_pursuit.US_surface_loss_bound: About 3 heavy cruisers sunk, about 2 cruisers heavily damaged, about 5-6 destroyers lost, several additional ships damaged. Exact named assignments remain pending roster-level adjudication.
surface_pursuit.Japanese_surface_loss_bound: About 1 heavy cruiser heavily damaged, about 2 destroyers lost, about 2-3 destroyers damaged, 1-2 Kongo-class ships light-to-moderately damaged. Exact named assignments remain pending roster-level adjudication.

tow_capture_salvage.Hornet: US towing is attempted or prepared but abandoned when speed/contact geometry makes it a trap. Japanese capture interest is real but limited to a short feasibility/technical inspection; trans-Pacific tow/capture is rejected. Portable equipment/observations may modestly accelerate later radar/CIC/damage-control learning, never an instant tech jump.
tow_capture_salvage.Saratoga_Enterprise: No practical tow/capture window once stopped; battle pressure and Midway air/submarine threat make immediate rescue or enemy capture infeasible.
tow_capture_salvage.Japanese_damaged_carriers: Soryu and Hiryu retain self-propulsion and withdraw under escort; no tow required on center line. Akagi/Kaga are beyond useful tow transition and are evacuated/then disposed of.

midway_reduction_and_landing.1942-06-11: Japanese carrier air attacks reduce sortie rate, fuel/maintenance/communications; US carrier aircraft that diverted to Midway keep the base dangerous but over-crowded and hard to sustain.
midway_reduction_and_landing.1942-06-11_12_gunfire: Yamato/other battleships and cruisers conduct stand-off bombardment. Computing benefits mainly reduce systematic error and solution-convergence time; they do not create laser-like dispersion. Fixed batteries, fuel, communications, runway sectors and command points are progressively suppressed.
midway_reduction_and_landing.1942-06-12_US_last_air_counterstrike: Remaining SBD/F4F/B-17 force attacks carriers/cruisers/transports; center Japanese additional aircraft losses about 8-12 and one cruiser/transport-class target may take a bomb hit. US loses/damages about 20-30 additional aircraft.
midway_reduction_and_landing.landing_1942-06-13: Reef and beach defenses remain real. Improved loading/landing reliability accelerates heavy-equipment/engineer/artillery availability but does not erase terrain. Eastern Island falls first; Sand Island requires repeated waves and night reinforcement.
midway_reduction_and_landing.capture: Organized US defense collapses about 1942-06-14 night to 06-15; Midway captured by Japan.
midway_reduction_and_landing.Japanese_ground_loss_bound: KIA/MIA about 500-750; WIA about 800-1100; total casualties roughly 1300-1800.
midway_reduction_and_landing.Allied_ground_loss_bound: KIA about 600-900; WIA about 700-1000; POW about 1500-2500. Some priority aircrew/personnel escape by PBY/other means before final collapse.

United_States.Pacific_fast_carrier_state: temporary zero before Wasp transfer; Ranger remains Atlantic unless strategic emergency forces reconsideration
United_States.aircrew_note: Hull losses are much larger than personnel losses; many experienced carrier aviators/deck/support personnel survive for later Essex/CVL force generation.

branch_implications: Historical WATCHTOWER/Guadalcanal timetable is invalid and must be rerun.
FS becomes much more attractive but cannot ignore 8-12 week Japanese carrier-airgroup rebuild and logistics/base preparation.
Midway should be operated as a relatively lean forward search/flying-boat/submarine-support and warning node, not as a giant permanent fleet base.
US immediate counter is submarine/air interdiction and Hawaii/Johnston/Palmyra defense, not rapid amphibious recapture.
Japan gains a large summer-autumn 1942 carrier-operational window, but also acquires long exposed logistics tails at Port Moresby/Solomons/Midway.
